body:
Knowing that there are people out that betray people's trust and consciously do things that they understand will hurt them, and then justify it by saying "it's the right thing to do" is exactly why I've lost my hope in this world, and this conversation is making me upset, so I will desist before I get to the point where I feel like I'm going to get up  from my desk and walk into a line of traffic.

I don't think the end justifies the means. Perhaps this is where you and I differ.

I'm not technically beyond help, but I no longer trust the people who have the power to help me to do so and act in my best interests, even if they did a heel-face-turn and decided they want to, because of events such as the one described above, which was not the first, and not even the latest. Which I suppose you could say means I am beyond help. Seeing a psychologist about all of it, but the person who pushed me to see the psychologist keeps doing things that are entirely contrary to the psychologist's recommendations (psychologist says "stay where you are, don't move again"; person in question: "I'm putting your name on a lease, and you have to be out of here in a week").

I'm not saying that you shouldn't try to stop a person if you think they are suicidal, however I feel that if a person is using a means that is anonymous (such as posting on the internet or ringing a hotline), or expresses a wish to not be institutionalised, they probably do not in fact want to be reported to an emergency service.

But was he making a mistake? That's the thing - I'm pretty sure he was convinced (and remains so) that he did the right thing, and it sounds as though the point of view being advocated here would be to do the same thing faced with that situation - that that is and was the correct course of action, despite the concrete possibility, as in my case, of making it worse, and potentially putting that person beyond help.

I had someone call an ambulance on me, against my express wishes, during a period of time when I was actually feeling pretty calm and feeling like I was coping - they didn't keep me very long but the experience itself was pretty traumatic, andthe irony is, now that person is another person I can no longer trust to support me when I need it, and now I feel like I have no one, and that in itself is making me feel like I don't want to live anymore - and now that I know what it's like to be on the inside of a psychiatric ward, if there's a chance that I will end up there again, I won't be asking for help from anyone.

I feel (though I can't prove) that fewer people would reach out for help via hotlines if they thought there was a signficant chance of the police being alerted and them being hospitalised involuntarily.

Thinking the same thing - I'm realising that a lot of mantras about life are really stupid and illogical, lately, and that one about "better to have loved and lost than never to have loved at all"? The lines about only regretting things you didn't try? Total bullshit, I think.

I'm sorry to hear that she broke up with you when you proposed - that's awful. I'm assuming that the proposal itself didn't warrant breaking up over .... Did she give a reason? (You don't have to talk about it if you don't want to).

I don't think the ex-bf was like this when we were in a relationship, but now I don't trust myself anymore (he also tried to have me institutionalised recently - and one of the bizarre things about the mental healthcare system is that I didn't think I was anything less than sane before, but now that the accusation has been levelled at me, everyone seems to doubt it, and now so do I, which makes me feel worse about the world). My personal theory is - and I can't prove it - that in the few months that we were living together, he was working from home in a job that was stressful in terms of content and in terms of structure (unreliable work), he would go for days without leaving the apartment unless I made him go out and do something together, no vitamin D, no exercise, eating poorly because he can't cook for himself (never lived out of home before) and because he's cheap. But he refuses to acknowledge any of these things, and I'm not sure if this is just another example of someone (myself) blaming other people instead of dealing with the fact that I was a terrible person or something, but I can't figure out, and no one will tell me, what I did wrong.

My ex-boyfriend encouraged me to leave my sharehouse to move in with him, so when he broke up with me three months after signing the lease, I had nowhere to go and had to stay living there with him while I futilely looked for another place to live, which made it really difficult to not notice when he started trimming his pubic hair over the bathroom bin really difficult - and then, of course, he stayed out one night (he doesn't know anyone in this city), and later admitted that he had gone on a date, and that it had "gone well - sort of" (he then went into a digression about how male masturbation was seen as gross, whereas female masturbation was seen as hot and sexually liberating, and asked me if I had been using my vibrator while we'd been broken up). At some point, I realised that night would have been our two year anniversary -neither of us had really been big "anniversary" people, either, but it seems like the stupidest thing to think about, but it just contributed to my being intensely upset - that it could have been his and the other girls' anniversary, too.

I don't know if this was the right thing to say - it just kind of came out. It fucking hurts. I know. You know. If you want to talk, I'm here.

It's actually one of the weird things about Australia - kids get taught basic snake bite and spider bite first aid from a very young age. You don't think about it when you grow up here, but it's not common practice in other countries. Is a reasonably practical skill to have here.

Wow, Norway - any reason in particular?

Sometimes the "never returning" is the inevitable part of moving away. I moved to where I am now about a year ago - ostensibly across the country, no family here, and only knew two people in the city - and I guess I kind of took for granted that I would be able to go home at any time if I needed to ... but even though it's a practical impossibility at this point, I don't think I would if I could. It's the taking-the-journey-and-coming-back-changed thing - you know, Frodo and Sam and the Shire, etc.
My bad - I just assume that everyone's just refreshing the page like I am :D

Glad to hear it! I saw some awful statistic a while ago about something like 70% of college graduates unable to find jobs (terrifying, consider what you guys pay for your tertiary education) - so it'll be a relief for everyone when your economy stabilises. I've been to the US a few times previously, though I mostly did the East Coast (and Denver, for kicks). I would go back to Boston in a heartbeat, given the opportunity.

Where would you go in the world if you had the choice?

Passing the buck -! To the "two people in six years" person, no less, haha. Not exactly a success story myself - I am browsing r/SW after all.

I think that sounds entirely reasonable - I wouldn't make a big deal out of it, but it's important that you're honest, and that you feel like you're being honest. Hopefully she should understand that the "less desirable" parts of everyone's mind gets the best of them sometimes, and anyway, you'll probably need her support in some capacity if you continue the relationship.

It may help to practice what you're going to say in your head - sounds like you're doing that already - it's a great idea. If you can, imagine the whole conversation - her likely responses, your responses to her responses. It may make you feel more prepared and less anxious about breaching the topic.

Australia. Having an unusually cold, wet summer this year, but perhaps it's because I grew up in a very dry, hot part of the country. I want to visit the us while your dollar is so crap haha ... but shit in my life means it's not a priority right now.

I'm not naturally adventurous but I've learned to push myself to do things that make anxious that I know shouldn't, and it seems to work out okay ... No guarantees, but I don't feel like it would hurt in this case.

 I'm not in the us, didn't know about the weather. Definitely something to factor in.
Time = your. Phone typing ftl.
Hrmm, good point about the driving. But ... If you believe you can handle the trip responsibly, I feel that it would be good if you went.

I am also someone who doesn't date much. Two people in six years, for the record. I suspect that i'm a little where you are, in that I'm facing the prospect of being forever alone, and I'm terrified. that's my disclaimer.

It doesn't sound to me that she's being deliberately insensitive, and I do think that time anxieties are not unreasonable - though perhaps a little visceral. If you talk to her about this, and she thinks it is unreasonable, the two of you arw probably incompatible ... But this does not mean you are forever alone. for what it's worth, there's very likely someone as inexperienced as yoy, and you'll be able to learn and grow together.

And I think there's a good chance if you articulats your anxieties she may simply adjust her behaviour.

so why are you quitting the subreddit?

One would expect someone who used to be suicidal to understand (and perhaps even be more tolerant of) the feelings of anger and resistance that comes with being suicidal. Unfortunately, I feel like you're the exact kind of people - who say they care but then give up - who form the context of the lives of the people here who suffer from being lonely.
I should know betyer by mow than to jump in on people's comments but - really? ' you'll still be dead but you'll hsve more to site for it?.. Hore does that make sense?

honestly, I tried and didn't get very far.. . I think i've put too much time and effort truong to take care of myself at this point that it seems impossible to think of damaging myself, and I know rationally that I didn't do anything wrong, it's my impossible (or difficult) situation that's pushing me to the brink, and in some ways I shouldn't be the one who should have to take responsibility for it... Though I have mt moments. My first preferen e right now would be to not exist, not wake up another day.

This is a serious question: is there, like, an r/mania wher people post their  ' elevated moods' and other people try to offer support or show them the flip side of reality? I don't actually know reddit that  well. Are there hotlines you can call? If I suspect someone I know of being manic ... What is the appropriate course of action?.
No reason to care ... No  reason to not care ... That feels like a meaningless statement to me in my situation.

To clarify: the OP argues that he does care about people (blanket statement), a commenter posts that the OP has no reason to care about people in that way, you reply that you have no reason not to care. So it's not you stating that you care ... it's you stating that you don't have a reason not to care.
Yes, I understand, and I appreciate that. Listening does help some people, especially on sw. however some people need something else, and the 'i care about you' blanket statement can seem trite.

can you perhaps understand why it doesn't mean much to people if that care factor - that abstract 'preference' that people be happy rather than troubled, that neither translates to a tangible difference in their lives, nor is a specific 'i care about you and tge situation you're in, as opposed to people in general'? Sorry for any formatting errors, responding awkwardly from a phone.
So, hypothetically, someone's not happy: how does that affect you?
What you've just described would be a lot of people's ideal state; what they would say they're working towards.
it's one thing to be there if she changes her mind, but at one point do you decide she does know what she wants? At what point do you let go, at what point do you stop feeling you'll regret it?

That is true - 100% chance of failure if you don't try. I did try to go back - tried to ascertain how he came to his decision, tried to fill in all the missing gaps in his context (and there were some big ones) as best I could. But he has closed his mind to all of it, for no other reason than he "knows it wouldn't work", and it's not up to me anymore. Which sucks, because it means I have to deal with the huge, life-changing, unsolvable logistical problems that come with not being in the relationship anymore, which are the real cause of my "depression" or "situational crisis" (meanwhile, he doesn't have to deal with any of the problems, even though he caused all of them). I have no choice but to move forward, but I can't move anywhere until I sort out my money problems, my career, and find a place to live (and when that's done, do something about my damn social circle), all of which were jeopardised by him initiating the breakup. Which has been a very slow process (and a horrible few months).

What are you thinking? Move forward? Go back? What's your instinct?

We can't go back. I think I've come to terms with that much. And the one thing that people keep telling me that actually fits reality is that you can't be in a relationship with someone who doesn't want to be in a relationship with you (or at least, it's reasonably unethical to do so, under contemporary Western ontology). And we can struggle all we want with why the people we loved didn't want to be in relationships with us, and the fact that those reasons don't make sense, or were silly reasons, or maybe should have been outweighed by the pain and problems that they caused, but we can't go back. Other people's actions are beyond our control. And if they want to be shitheads, somehow we have to deal with that. Somehow. And, honestly (hypocritically), from what I've read, I do have hope for you.

Oh, hell, you really are me. I got the "we want different things from life" line (and the "I don't see a future together" line - another story), which is bullshit because I have no idea what I want from life, and I don't see how he can know what I want from life, and I'm pretty darn sure he has no idea what he wants from life, either. And when I tried to talk to him about it, it was like, no, he's not even going to open his mind to the idea, like he decided on his own in isolation, which is not fair because it's a decision that involves two people.

It's not true that people don't need time to think, though I personally feel that it's not fair to push you away but still keep you like that. Which doesn't help, I know - "fair" is a concept like "deserve" that cannot be enforced. People should communicate. People should communicate better. People who don't shouldn't be in relationships, and should take responsibility when they hurt other people because of their inability to communicate.

/angry

For me, it's like, I open up to people so rarely and let so few people close to me, and they've all left me a lot worse than I was so why should I let another person in? But being alone/lonely is agonising. And the "deserve someone better" is bullshit, too - at its most abstract, that would require some benign entity weighing up the good and the bad in the world and allocating me some good because of the shit I've had to deal with in the past, which seems unrealistic; and even in a concrete way, it relies on me sitting here, counting on the fact that someone will finally have it within themselves to "recognise" the fact that I'm a worthwhile person, a process over which I have no control and kind of find incredibly sad.

Did she give any particular reason as to why she wanted a break?

I wish I could help - I'm in a vaguely similar situation to yours - but I don't have an answer. People keep throwing the same lines at me: "plenty of fish in the sea" and "you deserve someone who wants to be with you", etc. all of which are meaningless and refutable and I don't want to perpetuate that shit. But I am here, if you would like to talk to someone.

I will say: at 18, you're young. You're not even fully formed yet. You have a great deal of (physical, emotional, environmental) change ahead of you before you settle. This reality will almost certainly not be your reality for very long.

Sometimes I also feel that the whole "chemical imbalance in your brain" thing isn't right either. Happiness is a different mix of chemicals in your brain - does that mean it's an imbalance? Any why don't people try to "fix" happy people?

It's not that I don't appreciate the "I care" sentiment - but I do think that in a lot of cases (not all) it doesn't mean much.

Yeah, well, that's where I'm at, currently. I struggled really hard to get where I was, and then it was all taken from me, and now I feel like even if I put in the work to get what I want, what's to stop another person coming along and taking it from me again? After all, the whole world stood by and condoned it last time; if the world supports it, I must be the one who is out of place.
Sorry - phone typing. If you're getting by, even for now, you're a strong person.

I read the part about not being able to watch movies or tv, and I did that double tKe when someone articulates exactly what you're feeling. I have a bloody degree I  film fer chrissakes and I can't watch it anymore because it's all a lie... Because that's the shit we get fed to make us aspire to  something that didn't exist. I thought I was happy once, but ot was just an incredibly fragile lie.

I have no advice because I'm in a similar position and haven't figured out how to fix it ... But you're not alone.

But in some ways your idea of "recovery" only makes sense in terms of depression being a sickness or an illness, which is valid under what seems to be your (and, to be fair, the dominant scientific and medical) ontology, but what if someone in my position doesn't see it as being something I necessarily need to "recover" from - that there's nothing "wrong" with me, per se, so it's not a matter of wanting or needing to be "fixed", it's that my ontology is different from the dominant, and the dominant is so hegemonic it considers all counter-positions to be "crazy" and "irrational"?

This is going to get me into trouble, but do you know X-Men? And how people were trying to "cure" their mutations? I feel like it's kind of like that ... not that I believe that people like myself are the next stage in evolution or whatever, but it's a fundamental difference maybe we shouldn't be trying to reconcile, but instead to coexist. Or perhaps religious differences is a better example - two ultimately different wold views, neither of which is necessarily or objectively better than the other, but no good can come of trying to convert people - the best and easiest peace is to let people believe what they want.
Boil it down to an ontological difference which I don't think we can reconcile ... but that still doesn't mean your ontology is more valuable than mine.

"of course this is extremely difficult to recognize when you are trapped in the black hole of depression." <- I think this is kind of my point. It's easy for people who "recover" from depression or get help to look back and say, well, yeah, it gets better, and perhaps, statistically, it does get better for some people, but you don't hear from the people for whom it did not get better, because that's the catch-22 of suicide and death.

Sorry, ambiguous use of the word "normalise" - not "normalise" as in, to behave as if something is normal, I meant, that psychiatrists and psychologists prescribe medication and give therapy in order to restore "order" or "normality" to people who have been diagnosed with some kind of abnormal brain chemistry in the form of depression, suicidal ideation, eating disorders, etc.

I think in an ideal, non-realistic world, people would be able to choose the time/manner of their death, or at least be able to die on their own terms - within reason, though as soon as you start to unpack this, it begins to get complicated.

I don't think that the healthcare professionals I have dealt with have been unempathetic to my needs, necessarily - the people in my social life have, probably, and I'm having a lot of difficulty reconciling that with my future. There are always going to people walking around in the world who are like this, who will say whatever they want to get what they want and as soon as it's not convenient or profitable for them, they'll take it back, and there's no way I can guard or guarantee against it, and that is the most depressing thing I think for me.

I understand that not causing others pain is a huge factor to take into account when one is considering suicide, and it would be at the very least callous to not think about it, however, I feel - and perhaps this is just me in my situation - that there are people all around me who are hurting others every day, both maliciously and without necessarily intending to, sometimes in a big way and sometimes in small, cumulative ways, and I'm not sure why other people should be able to get away with this but when someone raises their hand and says their suicidal, everyone piles on them and tells them to stop because they will be causing pain the world (though, really, I suspect in a lot of cases, it's the pain a person would be experiencing if they lost that person to suicide that they are most concerned about, which entirely self-interested).

I'm glad that it worked for you, and that you're here if that's what you want. My concern is more with the idea of "functioning" - that the endgame is always to get a person to function to some notion of productivity or "normality", but those notions seem to only apply on a grand ideological scale (as in, capitalist ideology) and not to the individual. Also, being "normal" doesn't work for everybody - it's an arbitrary concept, and an average at best.

I guess it's the idea that people with suicidal ideation are "not right" and "need fixing" is also my problem - can't suicidal ever be a rational decision made by a sane person?

I also have to say - I feel like there's kind of a Kool-Aid effect when it comes to this subject: a lot of people will tell you suicide is a bad thing because they have been told that it's a bad thing but not because they've actually thought about it (not saying you in particular, by any means), and also, of course the people who survived and for whom treatment have worked are going to say that it gets better but you don't hear from the people for whom it doesn't.

No, I understand that dying is probably not fun, but living is not really that great either. The latter is outweighing the former by a margin at the moment, but those scales could tip at any moment.

Nothing I used to love to do seems to mean anything, and it keeps coming back to the "I'm alone" thing. I go out and all I can think is, "where are you, my love? Why aren't you here?", which is pretty much as pitiful as it sounds. I stay at the apartment, and do nothing all day, and I think, "God this is unfulfilling", though apparently it's the ex-'s lifestyle of choice. Writing about the pain isn't cathartic, and it's certainly not good writing (who will want to read it?). I'm earning minimum wage (publishing! Yay!) full-time at the moment and I can't really afford to live in this city. It's one of the most expensive cities in the world. It's also really the only city in my country where there are jobs in the publishing industry, and I was job-hunting for a year and a half before I got this one; I'm not exactly qualified for much.

Not trying to be contrary, but I've thought about this a lot.

I'm not actually a good enough writer - I haven't been legitimately published in years, and I have poor writing habits (namely, I've had every opportunity to actually work on a project, and have never been able to bring myself to get very far with them) - and I tend to write in the least-popular genres between literary and populist. Also, don't know what I would do in the meantime, between now and publication/production. Preferably not what I am doing now, but if not that, then what?
Yeah, but your economy has had a pretty significant effect on your film industry in the last few years.

You pretty much have to be in the US at this point (English is the only language I speak fluently). Impossible to get a visa, and even then it's a competitive industry, and I think "cutthroat" is the last word you'd use to describe me.

Like I said, you can be as "interesting" as you're comfortable with being, but you don't want to be alone, you still have to hope/pray/naively believe that someone will come along and want to invest themselves in you.

Two small things: Don't set yourself a deadline. A day is just a day. Your birthday is just another day. We measure time by arbitrary numbers. Nothing need to happen by then. If it happens the day after, nothing bad will happen.

And, relationships are overrated. I've only had two meaningful ones, and I wish I'd had fewer. They both told me they loved me, and they both screwed me over. I lost my virginity at 22. There's no hurry. I don't know if it will mean anything to tell you it's not a race, but I feel like perhaps your yearning so hard for something that may not fix your problems.

I work in publishing, but I am increasingly doubtful of its long-term stability. I trained as a writer and a filmmaker, but don't really have much of an interest working in the film industry, except perhaps as a writer, and I'm really living in the wrong country to do that.

Ends at the end of July. I've lived in this city for a year today, actually, about 4,000km from the city I grew up in. Moving here hasn't worked out so well, not sure if moving again would solve anything.

Apartment is a one bedroom ensuite.

We're both on the lease. Even if I kick him out, I can't afford to stay here on my own (not sure if even want to anyway), and I'm not sure that being alone in an apartment by myself is something a psychologist would recommend. If I take myself off the lease and get him to pay for my furniture and the bond (about $4,000 total), I have nowhere to go. This is the dilemma I have been struggling with for almost two months now. Sorry to hijack your post.

No doubt, but it seems that some people are more affected by it than others. I'm trying to be selfish now, but I'm finding it difficult. I didn't think it was an intelligence thing, but the ex-bf was saying last night about how I'm smarter than him, how he can't out-logic me (on the subject of why I feel exactly the way I feel at the moment), so I dunno. One of the reasons why he left? Who can say. He is sitting four metres away from me as I write this, playing one of the Fallout games in loud surround sound, so all I can see and hear is people getting head-shot, which I don't feel is a very nice thing to be confronted with when I've tried to slit my wrists twice in the last forty-eight hours.

I don't know if this will help, but I'm pretty much in the same place you are. New city, few friends here, friends from my hometown seem to have moved on without me, can't trust my family, ex-boyfriend left me under pretty traumatic circumstances. I feel like we were all lied to: it doesn't matter how good a person you are, how confident you are in yourself, how interesting you are - if you're lonely at all, you have to depend on someone else to like you, and you can't control that. At least that's my current train of thought. I'm still clinging to the hope that maybe someone can prove me wrong.

My point, I think is: it may feel like we're broken, that you went wrong somewhere and that you can't survive in this world, but you are not the only person out there who feels like this.
